proposal_cited: ORCH-R30 lane T21-a — the r28 close-out registration: the lexical-sensitivity census (which content words carry the mass)
claim: C38 — state-side noul mass is carried by a concentrated minority of question-echoing content words
floors: F1 the map byte-identical to E-Q25 (sha asserted); F2 states differ only at the sampled word occurrences (inverse-exact, pre-flight caught 4 application defects AM1-AM4 before any spend); F3 one batched call per (record,word), 12 answers, model_served per call; F4 the 4 anchors within band; F5 sealed r24/r28 baselines only; F6 the word map frozen at registration
bands: H1 breach rate < 30% AND top-20% share >= 50%; H2 echo rate >= 2x non-echo AND >= 3 echo breaches; H3 strict median ordering NOUN > VERB > IDENT; C38 = H1 AND H2

design: the census: 120 single-word near-synonym substitutions (TF-IDF top-6 per record, the frozen salience rule) + 4 anchors; movement vs the sealed r28 baseline (primary) and r24 (secondary); AM5 grid quantization before every comparison
llm: 125 typesafe calls (120 + 4 anchors + 1 flip canary), all jev-1.13.0

verdict: E-Q40 VERDICT (the lexical-sensitivity census — 120 single-word near-synonym substitutions over the sealed E-Q21 20-record corpus, one batched 12-question call each, the byte-identical E-Q25 map, all 124 calls jev-1.13.0, the flip canary NEGATIVE): C38 DIES — and the death is the round's finding: THE LEXICAL SENSITIVITY IS BROAD AND SHALLOW, NOT CONCENTRATED AND ECHO-DRIVEN. H1 DIES: the rate half lives (11/120 = 9.2% breach the 0.10 band — a minority of words) but the concentration half dies (the top 20% of words carry 45.3% of movement mass, under the registered 50% — the mass is diffuse, 2.27x uniform, not the predicted 2.5x+). H2 DIES DECISIVELY: THE ECHO LAW IS FALSE — words that lexically overlap the question-map text breach at 13.0% (3/23) versus 8.2% (8/97) for non-echo words (ratio 1.58x < 2x) and the class medians are IDENTICAL at 0.05; the strongest possible bridge — the word 'record', present in every one of the 12 question texts — moves 0.02 when removed from the state. THE READOUT IS NOT A KEYWORD MATCHER: it reads the record's whole lexical fabric. H3 DIES at the instrument's resolution (AM5): NOUN and VERB medians are both exactly 0.05 on the API's 2-decimal grid (the first unsealed run showed a spurious 8e-17 NOUN>VERB ordering — killed, not stretched); the receipt is TWO-TIER: content words 0.05 > identifiers 0.03. WHAT LIVES: P1 (max single-word movement 0.25 = 2.5x the band — one state word alone carries T1-scale mass); P2 (P8_exact the most-moved axis at mean 0.0248 — the THIRD independent instrument converging on the exactness axis as the noisiest seat); P3 (decoy floor 0.013625 over 480 readings — canary immunity extends to state-side word swaps); P4 (median shape Spearman 0.9762 — the profile shape survives single-word swaps better than T1's question-side rewording); P5 (IDENT the lowest median — identifiers are the floor; swapping experiment ids barely registers). P6 DIES (0/3 echo breaches landed on the word's echo axes — movement is NOT axis-targeted at the swapped word's semantic home; the breaches' argmax axes track the SUBSTITUTE's field at least as often: rebalancing->P4_alloc, check-tier->P8_exact, linkage->P1_nonlocal). The anchors: 0.02-0.03 vs the sealed r28 baseline — the drift band holds a FIFTH reading (the tightest yet). The mechanism receipt for the T1 decomposition: the question-side synonym mass was never 'a few load-bearing words' — it is the diffuse sum of many small state-side contributions, each individually mostly sub-band, with a shallow tail of 0.11-0.25 movers.
